'''Takekunihiko no Mikoto''' (武国彦命, birth and death dates unknown) was a [[Kofun period]] noble. He is also known as '''Takedainin no Mikoto''' (建大臣命) or '''Takeōomi no Mikoto''' (武大臣命).

== Overview ==
Takekunihiko no Mikoto is referred to by alternate names such as '''Takeōomi no Mikoto'''<ref>{{ill|Nakata Norinobu|ja|中田憲信|qid=DELETED_QID}}. "諏訪氏", in 『諸系譜』, Vol. 13.</ref> and '''Takedainin no Mikoto'''<ref>{{ill|Enkawa Kazuhiko|ja|延川和彦}}, "諏訪氏系図," in 『修補諏訪氏系図.正編』,飯田好太郎, 1921, p. 25.</ref>.

According to the traditions of the Suwa Shrine's Middle Shrine in {{ill|Hokuto, Yamanashi|en|Hokuto, Yamanashi|qid=Q825272|lt=Hokuto, Yamanashi}}, and the accounts in 『甲斐国史』, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, {{ill|Take Nunokawa Wake no Mikoto|ja|建沼河別命|lt=Takenumakawabete no Mikoto}} was granted lands in the western region for his contributions during the eastern expedition. His grandson, Dainin no Mikoto, was reportedly appointed as the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko}} of Suwa Province and established a shrine there.

In a manuscript of the {{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q133833194}}, there is mention of his appointment as Suwa no Kuni no Miyatsuko during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}, although some theories suggest this might be a mistaken reference to {{ill|Nasu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|那須国造}}.<ref>Yuichi Sato, 『シナノの国造勢力』.</ref>
